questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Course catalogue, exciting destination, possibility of receiving the Erasmus Grant to finance my stay

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
I found mobility-online as well as the OLA platform difficult to navigate and sign correctly. 
The University of Bologna has pretty alright information online. 
All bureaucratic parts of the exhange that depended on mail-correspondences went frustratingly slow (OLA, Erasmus Grant, Course selection).

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much. The University of Bologna (UNIBO) offers a online introductory presentation - but awfully late in the proces. A lot of information would have been reassuring to receive earlier in the proces.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There's an online helpdesk at UNIBO where you can receive bureaucratic help through video-calls. If you get impatient with waiting on emails, the online helpdesk might prove helpful

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy - but I might have been lucky. I received the number of a landlord in the city through a student who've gone to UNIBO the year before me.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Not anything in particular. It is more expensive, than what I expected of Italian prices...

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The registration into the university went easy, was well-guided and mostly online. 
The registration of courses were difficult. The course catalogue is updated very late. You will apply for forhåndsgodkendelse for courses, which will not be held. The university also offers the opportunity to "visit" a lot of courses in the first weeks before deciding on which to follow. This is both a blessing and a curse: you get a better idea of what courses you actually want to enrol in - but you also have to be in the limbo-registration and OLA-process longer.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You check in online upon arrival. You enrol in courses through an online platform (studenti-online). You furthermore do the exchange paperwork of forhåndsgodkendelse at KU and OLA between host and sending institution.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online helpdesk, email guidance

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I experienced the course selection process as a nightmare, yet I at last ended up getting access to all the courses I wanted to. Be patient, be aware that the process is slow, make sure to register your choice of class in Studenti-Online (also before receiving OLA). There will be - especially as a student of Humanities - overlapping courses. Getting an overview of your timetable and avoiding course-overlaps can be difficult.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Take advantage of the "shopping"-possibility. I was first enrolled in a few courses that I ended up swapping from (bc they were not what I thought they would be/ I didn't enjoy the teaching method/ prioritising between overlapping classes) because it was so fairly easy. 

I went to a few classes just to check them out and was super excited by the professors or course contents. Wonderful experience that it was possible to change to these courses (as it is not the case at UCPH).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I choose a lot of courses outside of my field of study (mostly took courses in sociology, while I study philosophy at UCPH). The level was appropriate. The one MA-class in philosophy I did attend was similar to UCPH in difficulty.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I found some professor liked to "rant" without citing their sources, arguing their case by research or similar. Other professors were immensely knowledgeable and inspiring.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
APPLIED POLITICAL SOCIOLOGY	
EPISTEMOLOGY (1) (LM)
POLITICAL ECOLOGY OF WORK
WOMAN AND SOCIAL SCIENCES - DONNE E SCIENZE SOCIALI	
WOMEN AND LAW - DONNE E GIURISPRUDENZA

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Political Ecology of Work is banging!!!! I loved prof. Leonardi's lectures. His way of combining research on class and climate was great. 
Epistemology was a classic course in analytical philosophy. Very well facilitated.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit Rome, vist Naples, visit Sicily, take walks around the area easily accessible by train, go to Club 2 Club festival in Torino, have spritz, eat out, go to Labas, go the Modernissimo, go for runs along the lake north of the city, join the running club

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Hinge
Learn just a bit of the language. I didn't. Such a shame. UNIBO even offers free language courses if you're just at a very moderate level upon arrival (or! do the intensive language course at UNIBO before semester starts, many people meet each other through there)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, the city is gorgeous, the pace of life when you're away from CPH-obligations

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be patient with bureaucracy
Take courses with E. Leonardi
Be brave enough to ask people to hang if you find them cool

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bologna likes to demonstrate, the professors offer great liberties choosing form of exam and the alike; you need to learn to find calmness outside the set structures of studieordninger and agreed-upon deadlines

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
I was lucky to have amazing flatmates
I really appreciated my class-mates in some classes

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Bureacracy
